proof:
Source: step 2 of the parent proof (“L_{n−1} … has Hⁿ(L_{n−1}) = 0”, n = m + 1). Simon uses this implicitly in (26)–(33) (chapter-06.txt lines 1841–1898) when decomposing Q over the open faces of L_n.

Notation. n := m + 1. By definition μHE[n] = c · μH[n] for a constant c (Measure.euclideanHausdorffMeasure is addHaarScalarFactor • μH[n]). So every μH[n]-null set is μHE[n]-null, and it suffices to prove μH[n](L_m) = 0, where L_m := {x ∈ ℝ^P : ∃ s ⊆ Fin P, P ≤ m + |s|, x_i ∈ ℤ ∀ i ∈ s}.

1. Countable cover. For s ⊆ Fin P and z ∈ ℤ^P put A(s, z) := {x : x_i = z_i ∀ i ∈ s}. If x ∈ L_m with witness s, then x ∈ A(s, z) for z_i := x_i (i ∈ s) and z_i := 0 otherwise. So L_m ⊆ ⋃_{s : P ≤ m + |s|} ⋃_{z ∈ ℤ^P} A(s, z), a countable union (finitely many s, countably many z). By countable subadditivity it suffices to show μH[n](A(s, z)) = 0 whenever P ≤ m + |s|.
2. Fix such s and z, and put r := P − |s| ≤ m. Let κ : Fin r → Fin P enumerate the complement of s. Define ψ : Euclid r → ℝ^P by ψ(t)_i := z_i for i ∈ s and ψ(t)_{κ(l)} := t_l. ψ is affine with an orthonormal linear part, hence an isometry and in particular Lipschitz, and A(s, z) = range ψ.
3. dimH(A(s, z)) = dimH(ψ '' univ) ≤ dimH(univ : Set (Euclid r)) (LipschitzWith.dimH_image_le) = r (dimH_univ_eq_finrank). Since r ≤ m < m + 1 = n, hausdorffMeasure_of_dimH_lt gives μH[n](A(s, z)) = 0.
4. By steps 1–3, μH[n](L_m) = 0, so μHE[m+1](L_m) = 0. The argument includes P ≤ m (then L_m = ℝ^P, with s = ∅ allowed in step 1) and P = 0. ∎
key_steps: Cover L_m by the countably many coordinate affine planes A(s, z) = {x_i = z_i (i ∈ s)} with P ≤ m + |s|, z ∈ ℤ^P.
Each A(s, z) is the range of an isometry from Euclid r with r = P − |s| ≤ m. Hence dimH A(s, z) ≤ r < m + 1, so μH[m+1](A(s, z)) = 0 (hausdorffMeasure_of_dimH_lt).
Countable subadditivity and μHE[m+1] = c·μH[m+1] give μHE[m+1](L_m) = 0.
